Holzbaurechner / Raised bed

Raised bed calculator

How many boards and posts you need for your raised bed, and roughly what the timber costs.

How the raised bed is built

The calculator assumes horizontal boards of 28 × 145 mm screwed to four corner posts on the inside. From 1.6 m long, middle posts are added and joined with a cross brace, so the soil does not push the long sides outwards.

Which timber is best?

Larch and Douglas fir are naturally resinous and last many years in the garden without preservative. Pressure-treated softwood is cheaper. For a vegetable bed it should be fully lined on the inside.

The right size

A width of up to about 1.2 m is easy to work from both sides. If the bed stands against a wall, 60 to 80 cm is better. A working height of 80 to 90 cm is kind to your back.

Building a raised bed step by step

  1. Choose the spot: a sunny, level place with at least six hours of sun a day is ideal. Running the long sides north to south gives both sides light.
  2. Prepare the ground: lift the turf and keep it, level the ground and lay fine galvanised rodent mesh that turns up a little at the edges.
  3. Set the posts: stand the corner and middle posts on paving slabs or blocks so that they do not touch the soil. Line them up with a spirit level.
  4. Screw on the boards: level the bottom course, then screw course after course to the inside of the posts. Use stainless steel screws and pre-drill larch and Douglas fir.
  5. Fit the liner: fix dimpled membrane to the inside walls with the dimples facing the timber, ending just below the top edge.
  6. Fill: in layers from coarse to fine, as described below.

Filling it: the layers

A classic raised bed is filled in layers. At the bottom, coarse material rots down slowly and supplies nutrients and warmth for years:

  • Bottom layer: branches, twigs and prunings, about a third of the height.
  • Next: the lifted turf, grass side down, then leaves or half-rotted compost.
  • On top: 20 to 30 cm of mature compost or raised bed soil for sowing and planting.

The material settles over the first few years. Top up with compost or soil every spring. To work out the volume, multiply length × width × height: a bed of 2 × 1 m and 80 cm high holds 1.6 m³. Most of it is taken up by the lower layers, so you only need bought soil for the top layer.

Frequently asked questions

How many boards do I need for a raised bed?
That depends on the height and the board width. With 145 mm boards and a height of 80 cm you need six courses, so 24 boards for a rectangular bed. The calculator shows the exact number for your sizes.
Do I need to line the raised bed?
Yes, dimpled membrane on the inside protects the timber from constant moisture and makes it last much longer. The dimples face the timber so that air can circulate.
How long does a larch raised bed last?
Lined on the inside and kept clear of the ground, larch often lasts ten years or more.

All timber sections are guide values and do not replace a structural calculation. Carports and patio covers may need planning permission and building regulations approval, and a structural engineer's check depending on where you live.
